title: Etale stacks on schemes over a localized base
statement: Let $g:S\to S'$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. On $\mathit{Sch}/S$ and $\mathit{Sch}/S'$ use categories fibred in groupoids, functors over the base, natural isomorphisms over the base, and etale stacks in the sense of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. In particular, a stack has sheaves of isomorphisms and effective descent for objects for jointly surjective etale covering families. Write $j:\mathit{Sch}/S\to\mathit{Sch}/S'$ for composition with $g$. The category $\mathit{Sch}/S$, regarded over $\mathit{Sch}/S'$ by $j$, is the discrete-fibre stack represented by $S$, denoted $h_S$. If $p:\mathcal F\to\mathit{Sch}/S$ is an etale stack, the same total category with projection $j p$ is an etale stack $j_!\mathcal F$ over $\mathit{Sch}/S'$, with its morphism $p:j_!\mathcal F\to h_S$. Conversely, if $\mathcal G$ is an etale stack over $\mathit{Sch}/S'$ and $q:\mathcal G\to h_S$ is a morphism of stacks, then the same total category with projection $q$ is an etale stack over $\mathit{Sch}/S$. These constructions are mutually inverse equivalences of $2$-categories. On the right a $1$-morphism of pairs is a stack morphism commuting with the maps to $h_S$, and a $2$-morphism is a natural isomorphism compatible with these maps. No algebraicity, finiteness or separation assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 04WV (lemma-localize-stacks), Constructions A and B in Tag 04WT (section-localize), applied to the big etale site of S' and the object S/S'. The statement is site-independent; here the covering families are etale as required by the project's stack convention.

proof.text: Identify $(\mathit{Sch}/S')/S$ with $\mathit{Sch}/S$: an object is $T\xrightarrow{a}S\xrightarrow{g}S'$, and arrows commute with $a$. A covering on either side is exactly a jointly surjective etale family of underlying schemes. The fibre of $j$ over $T/S'$ is the discrete groupoid of $S'$-maps $T\to S$; lifting $u:V\to T$ sends $a$ to $au$, and the required factorization is unique because arrows in the slice are underlying scheme arrows satisfying one equation. For any $T/S'$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-small-etale-representable-presheaf-sheaf] on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ to the $T$-scheme $T\times_{S'}S$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Its sections over $V/T$ are precisely the maps $a:V\to S$ with $ga$ the specified map to $S'$. Thus compatible local such maps glue uniquely. This proves effective descent for the objects of $h_S$. Its isomorphism presheaf between $a,b$ has a singleton value exactly where $a=b$, and is empty otherwise; the same uniqueness proves its sheaf condition. Hence $j$ is the represented etale stack $h_S$ in the convention of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids].

source.place: Tag 04WT (section-localize), first lemma and the hypothesis before Construction A; Tag 03O3 (lemma-representable-sheaf-fpqc), specialized by the cited small-etale representable lemma

proof.text: Check the fibred-in-groupoids condition for $jp$ directly from [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. If $p(x)=(T,a)$ and $u:V\to T$ is over $S'$, lift the slice arrow $(V,au)\to(T,a)$ by $p$; it is a lift over $u$ for $jp$. For arrows $\alpha:y\to x$, $\beta:z\to x$ and an underlying base arrow $v$ with $jp(\alpha)v=jp(\beta)$, write the structure maps of $p(x),p(y),p(z)$ as $a_x,a_y,a_z$. Since $a_y=a_xp(\alpha)$ and $a_z=a_xp(\beta)$, the displayed equality gives $a_yv=a_z$. Thus $v$ is an arrow of the slice, and the unique factorization required for $p$ is exactly the unique factorization required for $jp$. The same argument with uniqueness and the identity arrow shows that every functor over either base preserves these cartesian lifts. In particular $p:j_!\mathcal F\to h_S$ is a morphism of fibred groupoids.

source.place: Tag 04WT (section-localize), Construction A: verification of the fibred category axioms

proof.text: For the isomorphism sheaf of $j_!\mathcal F$, take objects $x,y$ over $T/S'$ with structure maps $a,b:T\to S$. An isomorphism over $V/T$ can exist only if $a|_V=b|_V$, since its image under $p$ is an arrow over $\mathrm{id}_V$ in the slice. Given compatible local isomorphisms on an etale cover of $V$, the representable-sheaf conclusion of step 1, using [lem-weil-pbc-small-etale-representable-presheaf-sheaf] for $V\times_{S'}S$ [def-pc-fibre-product], gives $a|_V=b|_V$. All the local isomorphisms now belong to the isomorphism presheaf in $\mathcal F$ over the single $S$-scheme $(V,a|_V)$. Its sheaf condition, part of the stack hypothesis as defined in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], gives one unique isomorphism over $V$. Uniqueness in $\mathcal F$ also gives uniqueness in the unchanged total category. This proves the required sheaf condition, including covers on which there are no sections.

source.place: Tag 04WT (section-localize), Construction A, omitted verification: isomorphism sheaves

proof.text: Let $\{T_i\to T\}$ be an etale cover over $S'$ with a descent datum $x_i,\phi_{ij}$ in $j_!\mathcal F$. Write $p(x_i)=(T_i,a_i)$. Applying $p$ to $\phi_{ij}$ gives $a_i\operatorname{pr}_1=a_j\operatorname{pr}_2$ on $T_i\times_TT_j$. By [lem-weil-pbc-small-etale-representable-presheaf-sheaf] for $T\times_{S'}S$ [def-pc-fibre-product], there is a unique $S'$-map $a:T\to S$ with these restrictions. The same $x_i,\phi_{ij}$ are therefore an etale descent datum for $\mathcal F$ over $(T,a)$; no change is made to their overlap maps or cocycle equation. Its effectivity, as in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], supplies $x$ over $(T,a)$ and the specified compatible local identifications. The object $x$ is also over $T/S'$ under $jp$, and these identifications realize the original datum. Together with steps 2 and 3 this proves that $j_!\mathcal F$ is an etale stack.

source.place: Tag 04WT (section-localize), Construction A, hint: use that h_U is a sheaf to glue morphisms to U

proof.text: Conversely let $r:\mathcal G\to\mathit{Sch}/S'$ and $q:\mathcal G\to h_S$ be as in the statement, so $jq=r$. For $q(x)=(T,a)$ and a slice arrow $u:(V,b)\to(T,a)$, lift the underlying arrow by $r$ to $y\to x$. Since $q$ is over $\mathit{Sch}/S'$, the image of this lift has underlying arrow $u$, so $q(y)=(V,au)=(V,b)$. This is a lift for $q$. If $\alpha:y\to x$, $\beta:z\to x$ and $v:q(z)\to q(y)$ obey $q(\alpha)v=q(\beta)$, the unique-factorization condition for $r$ supplies a unique $c:z\to y$ over the underlying arrow of $v$. The arrows $q(c)$ and $v$ in the slice have the same source, target and underlying arrow, hence are equal. This is precisely the unique-factorization condition for $q$ from [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Thus $q$ is fibred in groupoids over $\mathit{Sch}/S$.

source.place: Tag 04WT (section-localize), Construction B: verification of the fibred category axioms

proof.text: For $x,y$ over $(T,a)$, their isomorphisms over $(V,a|_V)$ in the $q$-fibre are exactly their isomorphisms over $V$ in the $r$-fibre: the only slice arrow above $\mathrm{id}_V$ with these endpoints is the identity. Hence the isomorphism sheaf condition for $\mathcal G$ proves it for $q$. For an etale descent datum over a cover $\{T_i\to T\}$ of $(T,a)$, effectivity for $r$ gives $x$ over $T$ and local isomorphisms to the specified $x_i$. Write $q(x)=(T,b)$. Applying $q$ to these local isomorphisms gives $b|_{T_i}=a|_{T_i}$. The uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-small-etale-representable-presheaf-sheaf], applied to $T\times_{S'}S$ [def-pc-fibre-product], gives $b=a$. Thus the descended object and its local isomorphisms are over the required $S$-scheme. This verifies both stack axioms of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] for $q$.

source.place: Tag 04WT (section-localize), Construction B: descent for morphisms and objects

proof.text: On 1-morphisms use the unchanged total functor, and on 2-morphisms use the unchanged natural isomorphism [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. A functor $H:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$ over $\mathit{Sch}/S$ satisfies $p'H=p$ and hence $jp'H=jp$; this is exactly a functor of the resulting pairs over $\mathit{Sch}/S'$ commuting with their maps to $h_S$. Conversely that commuting equation says it is over $\mathit{Sch}/S$. A natural isomorphism is over the slice precisely when its components project to the slice identities, which is exactly the compatibility with the maps to $h_S$ required on the right. Identity, vertical composition, and horizontal composition are unchanged because they are the same functors and component maps in the same total categories. Starting with $p$ gives first $(\mathcal F,jp,p)$ and then $p$ again; starting with $(\mathcal G,r,q)$ gives $q$ and then $(\mathcal G,jq,q)=(\mathcal G,r,q)$. The composites are identities on objects, 1-morphisms and 2-morphisms, proving the claimed mutually inverse equivalences.

lean.statement: theorem etaleStack_localization {S S' : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}} (g : S ⟶ S') : IsModuliStack (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (Over.map g)) ∧ IsRepresentedByScheme (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (Over.map g)) (Over.mk g) ∧ (∀ F : BasedCategory.{v₁, w₁} (Over S), IsModuliStack F ↔ IsModuliStack (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (F.p ⋙ Over.map g))) ∧ (∀ (G : BasedCategory.{v₁, w₁} (Over S')) (q : BasedFunctor G (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (Over.map g))), IsModuliStack G ↔ IsModuliStack (BasedCategory.ofFunctor q.toFunctor)) ∧ (∀ (F : BasedCategory.{v₁, w₁} (Over S)) (F' : BasedCategory.{v₂, w₂} (Over S)), IsModuliStack F → IsModuliStack F' → ∃ E : BasedFunctor F F' ≌ ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (fun h : BasedFunctor (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (F.p ⋙ Over.map g)) (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (F'.p ⋙ Over.map g)) ↦ h.toFunctor ⋙ F'.p = F.p), (∀ f : BasedFunctor F F', (E.functor.obj f).obj.toFunctor = f.toFunctor) ∧ (∀ f, (E.inverse.obj f).toFunctor = f.obj.toFunctor) ∧ (∀ (f h : BasedFunctor F F') (α : f ⟶ h), HEq ((E.functor.map α).hom).toNatTrans α.toNatTrans) ∧ (∀ (f h) (α : f ⟶ h), HEq (E.inverse.map α).toNatTrans α.hom.toNatTrans))

reviewed_lean.note: First stage-2 delivery; only the item lean field and the new module EtaleStackLocalization.lean changed. Statement checked clause by clause against the node and Stacks 04WT/04WV. h_S = ofFunctor (Over.map g) is stated as IsModuliStack and IsRepresentedByScheme (Over.mk g). Constructions A and B are iffs on the same total category; each reverse direction is the opposite construction (q := ⟨F.p, rfl⟩, resp. q.w), so they are true. The hom-category equivalence BasedFunctor F F' ≌ {h | h ⋙ F'.p = F.p} is pinned by four normalizations to the identity on functors and NatTrans, so it is not arbitrary. BasedNatTrans between CFGs are isos, and h_S-compatibility is automatic by faithfulness of Over.map. Strict commuting = up to 2-iso since h_S is discrete. Edge cases g=id, S empty, a≠b and universes (shared u, free total universes) are OK; no extra hypotheses. Sorry only, no definitions; docstrings carry source, blueprint and the 7 steps; lean.statement is verbatim; stmt_deps are correct; the proof-only import has a published olean. No duplicate in Mathlib or the project; the report sections are present. No compile (no change).
